source.title: Bad Global Minima Exist and SGD Can Reach Them
source.authors: Sheng-Chao Liu; Dimitris Papailiopoulos; D. Achlioptas

record.file_problem: Text includes the full paper and appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports that vanilla SGD can fit natural labels yet generalize poorly after random-label pretraining, and that regularization, data augmentation, or momentum can mitigate the effect. This qualifies the claim that standard SGD's implicit bias alone explains good generalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results from training on random labels as an initialization, then training on true labels. It does not report held-out performance while labels remain random. Figure-only results are retained only where the text gives a qualitative description; cited prior work is not treated as a result.
record.test_reason: The study provides evidence on V1's coexistence of random-label fitting capacity and natural-label generalization in additional architectures and datasets. Its main initialization experiment addresses a different claim: whether SGD reliably escapes models pretrained on random labels. V1 does not assert independence from initialization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that random-label pretraining can lead vanilla SGD to models fitting true training labels perfectly while generalizing substantially worse, and that regularization, augmentation and momentum help escape these initializations. They argue this demonstrates a role for regularization in search dynamics; the precise mechanism remains open.
record.recipe_differences: Uses random-label pretraining as an adversarial initialization followed by standard SGD training on true labels; compares vanilla SGD with combinations of data augmentation, L2 regularization, and momentum. This is not a direct replication of the listed studies' procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization (random versus random-label-trained adversarial); data augmentation, L2 regularization, and momentum; replication factor R. The paper reports that increasing R degrades vanilla SGD test performance while SOTA SGD remains essentially unaffected.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-label pretraining lowers subsequent natural-label test accuracy under vanilla SGD, by up to 40% as described by the authors, despite near-perfect training fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Natural-label generalization under vanilla SGD depends on initialization; fitting training labels does not guarantee comparable test performance across initializations.

fits_no_version.finding: Augmentation, L2 regularization and momentum mitigate initialization damage; the full recipe produces nearly equal test accuracy across initializations. Increasing replication factor R worsens vanilla SGD while leaving SOTA SGD essentially unaffected.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training heuristics can help SGD escape the detrimental effects of random-label pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: Adversarially initialized vanilla-SGD models have larger weight norms and greater FGSM vulnerability; SOTA training reduces these properties.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight norms and input-perturbation robustness accompany initialization-dependent differences in generalization in these experiments.

record.problems: Test-accuracy curves are primarily presented as figures, with exact per-model values not supplied in the text. Table 2 gives detailed results for only ResNet18 on CIFAR10. The main experiments use five random seeds; the described adversarial initialization reaches 100% random-label accuracy except that some architectures are trained until convergence when they cannot. The study does not measure random-label held-out accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports figure results for training accuracy, replication factor R, model norms, and FGSM robustness, but these do not directly measure the held-out natural-label behavior specified in V1 or another listed version. No separate rows were added for them; qualitative test-accuracy results across the full model/dataset grid are summarized in R1 and R2. Figure 4's exact values are figure-only and not described numerically.

untested.parts: Held-out accuracy while labels remain random is not measured. Random-label fitting is described procedurally, with an unspecified architecture-dependent convergence exception, rather than reported quantitatively by architecture. The original architectures are not replicated.
No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness measure or ranking against generalization gaps. Weight norms and FGSM input robustness measure different quantities.
No removal of examples selected by label memorization influence.

record.verdict_notes: The proposed V1 limits_scope verdict confuses coexistence with initialization invariance. Lower accuracy can still satisfy V1's far-above-chance criterion. The SOTA recovery result also does not establish the matched unregularized recipe specified by V1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report held-out accuracy with random labels still in place; random-label fit is used to create an initialization. Tests whether subsequent standard training on natural labels generalizes similarly from that initialization.
